## The checker's report

Check of the design sheet of `fruit-slicer` (Fruit Slicer, band 9 to 12), round 1, file `fruit-slicer-r1.md` (copy of commit c4a4b134), everything above `## The look`.

Records: all 13 named records and `us-ca 6.NS.6.c` exist; code, standing, regime (`nl 10 B d`: 2026) and check state (every one `confirmed`) are as the lookup prints today.
Limits: each "Limits taken" line was read against that record's Limits; three lines hold something that is not there or leave a part untold (findings 4 to 7), the rest match.
Levels: levels, basis (`derived`; `convention`), sub-bands, both California gap lines, the Dutch gap line and both lane labels are as printed for ages 9, 10, 11 and 12; what the sheet says about ages 9, 11 and 12 in California is incomplete (finding 3).

Findings

1. **The claim, line 231.** Rulings 7 and 9: nine records are taken only in part and the claim does not say so, and it does not say from which jurisdiction the comparison signs, the parts beyond half and quarter, and the plain cut are taken. Replace the paragraph with:
"Fruit Slicer is designed from four content standards adopted by the California State Board of Education for grade 4 and grade 5 mathematics: `us-ca 4.NF.1`, `us-ca 4.NF.2`, `us-ca 4.NF.3.a`, and in part `us-ca 5.NF.4.a` (a fruit or a piece seen as equal parts of which some are taken; no product is named and no chain of operations is asked for). For the Netherlands it is designed from six goals of SLO's guidance for fase 2 and fase 3, which is guidance and not law: `nl rw/bew/6/01/fase2`, and in part `nl rw/gb/5/01/fase2` (without doubling), `nl rw/verh/1/02/fase2` (of a whole, not of a quantity), `nl rw/bew/6/02/fase3` (a part of a length, placed by eye; never the whole from a part), `nl rw/gb/5/05/fase3` (equal shares made in pieces; no row is asked for or written) and `nl rw/gb/5/06/fase3` (comparing and giving a place; nothing is put in order). It is also designed in part from one item of the legal core goals of 2026, `nl 10 B d` (comparing, with the reason shown; no ordering, and simplifying only as far as two names for one length), and from two statements of the legal reference level 1F, one in part (comparing only, with no number line) and one on the notation with a horizontal bar; those three are end-of-primary goals. The signs for less than, equal and greater than are taken from the California records alone: no Dutch record the game names carries them. The parts beyond half and quarter follow the California list and are, on the Dutch side, the game's own choice. For California the plain cut of one share from one fruit rests on the `grade-5` record alone. Every record named was confirmed when the lookup was read on 2026-10-03."

2. **The claim, line 233.** It says more than line 56 gives: the trial was on a line from 0 to 1 with written fractions, and the strip as built has none. Replace with:
"It is built on a representation taken from one with evidence behind it for fraction size: an estimate on a line followed by the true place beside it. The strip with a pictured share, as built here, is school practice and has no trial of its own. It makes no claim about what a child who plays it has reached."

3. **The records, us-ca, line 187.** Ruling 7 and the age rule (no record of the grade above or below without saying it is not the child's grade): `grade-5` is one of an eleven-year-old's two levels, not a level below, and nothing says that the plain cut rests on a `grade-5` record, which the lookup does not return at age 9. Replace the paragraph with:
"No `grade-6` record is named. The fraction statements of that level that the game could touch place numbers of either sign on a number line (`us-ca 6.NS.6.c`, confirmed), and the game has a strip and no number line. So for a twelve-year-old in California every record named is of a level below the one the lookup returns for that age, which is not the child's grade. For an eleven-year-old `us-ca 5.NF.4.a` is of `grade-5`, one of the two levels returned, and the three `grade-4` records are of the level below. No `grade-4` record is named for the plain cut, one share of one fruit in one piece: that part rests on `us-ca 5.NF.4.a` alone, so for a nine-year-old in California, for whom the lookup returns `grade-4` only, it is designed from a record of the level above, which is not the child's grade."

4. **The records, us-ca, lines 178 to 179.** Ruling 9: the game takes one reading of this record only, and "here it is applied to one fruit or to one piece" is not in its Limits. Replace both lines with:
"- `edu.us-ca.grade-5.mathematics.objective.5-nf-4-a` (`us-ca 5.NF.4.a`): state-board-adopted-standard, confirmed. Taken in part: a share of a fruit is found by seeing the fruit as so many equal parts and taking some of them, and the cut is placed where those parts end. The roller on a piece does the same to a piece. The game names no product and asks for no chain of operations.
  Limits taken: one of the two things multiplied is a fraction, and the other is a whole number or a fraction. The game's own choice within that: the other is one fruit, or one piece. Left open by Limits: the statement gives no list of denominators, so the parts in play are the game's own choice (below). Mixed numbers are not named in this part, so the boa's order is not designed from this record."

5. **The records, us-ca, line 183.** Ruling 9: "both of one same whole" is in this record's Summary and not in its Limits, and the rule for which pairs are laid out is the game's, not a limit. Replace the line with:
"  Limits taken: the same list of denominators; two fractions at a time, the result written with the sign for less than, equal or greater than; the ways of comparing named in the statement are examples; thirds against fifths have no common parts on the list. Not in Limits: that both fractions are parts of one same whole stands in the record's Summary, and the game keeps it: the cat's two tickets are always of the same fruit. The game's own choice: a pair is laid out only when the parts both can be ruled into are on the list."

  Limits taken: six concepts are listed, and half and quarter are the only fractions named; the wording does not mention notation; an offer for the band, with no year."

7. **The records, nl, lines 201 to 202.** Ruling 9: the record names half and quarter of a whole and of a quantity and the game takes the first only; and three quarters is first ordered at `quarter` in one piece, not "as three quarter pieces". Replace both lines with:

Taken in part: half and a quarter of a whole, found by dividing a fruit up for a customer. Half and a quarter of a quantity, which the record also names, are not in the game.
  Limits taken: two fractions, half and quarter, each of a whole and of a quantity; concrete situations of dividing up; no number range for the quantities; notation is not mentioned. The game's own choice: three quarters, ordered from `quarter` on, goes one step past the two fractions named."

8. **Where the two differ, line 222.** "Stay inside both sets" contradicts line 202 (three quarters is past the Dutch records), and "named on the Dutch side only by an end-of-primary record" is a statement about the whole pack that the sheet's records do not carry (ruling 1). In those four positions the fractions are half and quarter, which both sets carry, and three quarters, which on the Dutch side is the game's own choice. For a nine-year-old in the Netherlands the written fraction goes beyond the `fase-2` records; among the Dutch records the game names, the notation itself is named only by an end-of-primary record."

The game follows the California list, less hundredths, in the order halves, quarters, eighths, thirds and sixths, fifths and tenths, twelfths. 13. **The designed order, lines 116 to 118.** The three outcomes leave out a customer fed by hand, which line 156 names as a cause of the serve (the glider included), so the game's own call is incomplete; and "before that tin opened" lets a piece trimmed against an earlier open tin count as cut by eye, against the Guess answer on line 71. Replace the three lines with:
"- **Well**: the tin shut on a fit, and every piece in it was cut while no tin stood open, on a fruit the roller had not marked.
- **Mixed**: the tin shut on a fit, but a piece in it was cut while a tin stood open, or carries roller marks; or the customer was fed by hand, whatever it was fed, the glider included.
- **Badly**: the customer was sent off with a tin that held a misfit."

14. **The designed order, line 120, and What is stored, line 130.** One of the two who wait always carries a new thing, so after the position moves the one still waiting carries the new thing of the position before, and as written a cycle with it moves the position a second step on the same idea. Replace line 120 with:
"Only a cycle with the customer who carries the new thing of the position as it stands when the cycle is judged moves the position: up one after well, down one after badly, not at all after mixed. A customer laid out with the new thing of another position, who was still waiting when the position moved, moves nothing. A customer's taste never enters the judgement. A position moves between cycles, one step at a time, and no clock is read."
Replace line 130 with:
"- `window`: the customer at the window, or none: who it is, which fruit, the share or two shares ordered, the id of the position whose new thing it carries, or none, and whether its ticket is written and has part lines."
